html:
The kingdom centred on Lopburi in central Thailand, called Lavo in old sources, shown on the map in 1100. Lopburi lies on the Lopburi river, north of where Ayutthaya would later rise. For its early centuries see also Lavo.

Lavo began as one of the Mon Buddhist city-states of the Dvaravati culture. Chronicles say it sent the princess Camadevi north to found Haripunjaya, and the two states later fought each other. From the 11th century Lavo came under the Khmer Empire and became its main base in the Chao Phraya basin. Khmer style temples such as Phra Prang Sam Yot date from this time, and Khmer ideas of kingship later shaped the Thai court.

As Angkor weakened in the 13th century, Lavo acted on its own again. Its lands and court culture passed to the new kingdom of Ayutthaya, founded in 1351 just to the south.
